page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-24xCPU-256GB is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 24 shared vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 10.67 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks indicate a balanced profile with specific trade-offs. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is positioned in the bottom 10 percent, reflecting the shared CPU allocation and 2.0 GHz clock speed. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performs strongly, placing in the top 25 percent. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks consistently register average performance, though the Passmark memory score is classified as weak.

This instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require dedicated, high-frequency CPU cores. The high RAM-to-vCPU ratio makes it suitable for large-scale caching, in-memory databases, and data processing tasks. It is well-suited for workloads such as Redis deployments, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression tasks, whereas single-threaded applications or heavy LLM text generation may experience performance limitations.
